note: Selective VEGFR-1/2/3 TKIs in refractory, biomarker-unselected metastatic CRC: fruquintinib is the approved member; tivozanib and rivoceranib have only phase 2 CRC data.
label: Colorectal (VEGFR TKIs)

engagement.judgement: Opens the strip: the class's PD readout (VEGFR2 phosphorylation in tumour endothelium) existed in 2006; no tivozanib human study reporting a matching PD readout was found (DCE-MRI phase I not located).
engagement.model: Human tumour xenografts in athymic rats (KRN951/tivozanib)
engagement.note: Tivozanib (KRN951) lowered tumour-endothelial pVEGFR2 and microvessel density in rat xenografts; no human pVEGFR2 or vascular readout was published for comparison.
engagement.short: Rat xenograft pVEGFR2 fell; no human readout
engagement.quote: Following p.o. administration to athymic rats, KRN951 decreased the microvessel density within tumor xenografts and attenuated VEGFR-2 phosphorylation levels in tumor endothelium.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Sun 2014. The statement is a PK-to-threshold inference, not a measured human PD readout; no fruquintinib trial reporting sVEGFR2, plasma VEGF or pVEGFR2 was found.
engagement.judgement: Kept untested rather than same: the model's readout (pVEGFR2) was never measured in dosed humans; the exposure-above-threshold comparison is scored in the dose cell instead.
engagement.note: Human target suppression was inferred from phase I PK against the mouse >85% pVEGFR2-inhibition threshold; no PD readout was measured in patients.
engagement.short: Human suppression inferred from PK only
engagement.quote: at the maximum tolerated dose of once daily oral administration fruquintinib achieved complete VEGFR2 suppression (drug concentrations were maintained above that required to produce >85% inhibition of VEGFR2 phosphorylation in mouse) for 24 hours/day
engagement.reason: No human PD readout; PK inference only

dose.judgement: Opening entry; the FDA tivozanib review (2021) lists HT29, SW620 and COLO205 nude-mouse studies and TGI at 0.2-1 mg/kg/day in nude rats, but no stated human exposure target.
dose.model: Human tumour xenografts in athymic rats (KRN951/tivozanib)
dose.note: KRN951 shrank colon and other xenografts in rats; no human exposure target was stated or compared.
dose.short: Rat efficacy dose; no human comparison
dose.quote: It also displayed antitumor activity against a wide variety of human tumor xenografts, including lung, breast, colon, ovarian, pancreas, and prostate cancer.

dose.magnitude_basis: human trough concentration vs mouse concentration giving >85% pVEGFR2 inhibition; the abstract gives no numeric ratio
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Sun 2014; phase I (Cao 2016, 5 mg QD 3/1 recommended) and the 2017 phase II PFS result verified separately. Animal toxicology stated no tolerated margin above the effective dose (dog findings from 0.2x the clinical dose on BSA), so margin_stated is false.
dose.judgement: Dated 2014 because the model-to-human exposure comparison was public then; sufficiency ('was it enough') was shown by the 2017 placebo-controlled phase II and does not change the status. Decision 16 not applied: the tox package placed no NOAEL above the effective dose.
dose.note: At the phase I MTD, human fruquintinib concentrations stayed above the mouse >85% pVEGFR2-inhibition level all day; 5 mg 3/1 later proved sufficient (phase II, FRESCO).
dose.short: Human MTD exposure cleared mouse threshold
dose.quote: at the maximum tolerated dose of once daily oral administration fruquintinib achieved complete VEGFR2 suppression (drug concentrations were maintained above that required to produce >85% inhibition of VEGFR2 phosphorylation in mouse) for 24 hours/day
dose.reason: Target exposure reached at tolerated dose

dose.model: Simcyp PBPK model of fruquintinib (CYP3A victim and P-gp/BCRP perpetrator DDI)
dose.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: the review does not date the applicant's PBPK report (HUMP-2-B); the clinical DDI study it was fitted on (NCT04557397) was first posted 2020-09-21, so the model was built 2021-2023.
dose.note: Applicant's Simcyp model built to predict fruquintinib exposure under CYP3A modulators and its effect on P-gp/BCRP substrates.
dose.short: PBPK DDI model filed with the NDA
dose.quote: The Applicant conducted PBPK analysis to assess DDI potentials of fruquintinib as a victim when coadministered with CYP3A4 modulators and as an inhibitor when coadministered with P-gp and BCRP transporter substrates.
dose.judgement: In-silico dose model, a separate system from the animal PK/PD track; opener at first public use.

dose.model: Simcyp PBPK model of fruquintinib (CYP3A victim and P-gp/BCRP perpetrator DDI)
dose.magnitude_basis: simulated vs observed fruquintinib AUC ratio in healthy subjects: rifampin 0.34 vs 0.35 (Sim/Obs 0.97), itraconazole 1.18 vs 1.1 (Sim/Obs 1.07); FDA Table 76
dose.population: Healthy subjects in the CYP3A DDI study (NCT04557397); label population is refractory mCRC
dose.confidence_note: Quote verbatim in the bundled 217564 Multidiscipline review (Appendix 20.4). NCT04557397 has no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov, so registry_date is null.
dose.note: FDA: the model, fitted on the itraconazole study and verified on rifampin, reproduced both DDI results and was relied on for the untested efavirenz dosing statement.
dose.short: PBPK reproduced rifampin and itraconazole DDI
dose.quote: The model captured the observed fruquintinib PK changes when coadministered with itraconazole (AUCR was 1.1) and rifampin (AUCR was 0.35), a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor and a strong CYP3A4 inducer, respectively.
dose.judgement: Retrodiction, not same: fmCYP3A4 was refined on the itraconazole result and rifampin served as the verification set, both known before the model was finalised. Its one prospective prediction (efavirenz, AUC 68% of baseline) became the label's no-dose-adjustment statement for moderate CYP3A inducers without a clinical study, a regulator reliance on the in-silico model that stays untested in humans, so no fresh entry. The model concerns exposure under co-medication, not the efficacy exposure target; filed under dose as the brief's in-silico dose-choice case and flagged for the checker.
dose.reason: FDA: PBPK captured both clinical DDI results

efficacy.judgement: Model-first-use year for the track; the tivozanib NDA review lists HT29, SW620 and COLO205 nude-mouse xenograft studies (951-25, 951-06, 951-05).
efficacy.model: Human CRC cell-line xenografts in nude rodents
efficacy.note: Colon cancer xenografts in athymic rats responded to tivozanib (KRN951); no CRC patient result existed to compare.
efficacy.quote: It also displayed antitumor activity against a wide variety of human tumor xenografts, including lung, breast, colon, ovarian, pancreas, and prostate cancer.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: dose-dependent tumour growth inhibition in HT-29 mice (from 0.77 mg/kg) vs PFS hazard ratio; not commensurable
efficacy.confidence_note: Phase II abstract and FDA review (FRESCO, FRESCO-2) read in full for the quoted numbers; Sun 2014 model side at abstract level, HT-29 detail from the 2023 FDA review (xenograft activity from 0.77 mg/kg).
efficacy.judgement: BATON-CRC (tivozanib + mFOLFOX6 vs bevacizumab + mFOLFOX6, 2016) is not scored as contra: the xenograft predicted activity versus no VEGF blockade, and the trial tested superiority over an active same-pathway comparator (PFS 9.4 vs 10.7 months, ORR 45% vs 43%), which the model never predicted; recorded in patient_trials. Rivoceranib's 2019 single-arm phase II (PFS 3.9 months) has no control and no CRC-specific preclinical model was found before it (Tian 2011 abstract names no tumour types; a 2020 CRC xenograft paper would be a retrodiction and was not verified beyond its title). Outcome_tested positive: the PFS surrogate was followed by two positive OS trials.
efficacy.model: Human CRC cell-line xenografts in nude rodents
efficacy.note: HT-29 mouse xenografts predicted activity; placebo-controlled phase II met its PFS primary endpoint (HR 0.30); FRESCO and FRESCO-2 later confirmed on overall survival.
efficacy.short: Phase II PFS HR 0.30 vs placebo
efficacy.quote: PFS was significantly improved with fruquintinib plus BSC (4.73 months; 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.86-5.59) versus placebo plus BSC (0.99 months; 95% CI 0.95-1.58); (hazard ratio [HR] 0.30; 95% CI 0.15-0.59; P < 0.001).

patient_trials.quote: The median OS was 7.72 versus 5.52 months (HR 0.71; 95% CI 0.38-1.34).
The OS HR was 0.65 (95% CI: 0.51, 0.83; p<0.001) with a median OS of 9.3 months (95% CI: 8.2, 10.5)
The OS HR was 0.66 (95% CI: 0.55, 0.80; p<0.001) with a median OS of 7.4 months (95% CI: 6.7, 8.2) in the fruquintinib arm and 4.8 months (95% CI: 4.0, 5.8) for the placebo arm.

A prespecified interim futility analysis demonstrated that the futility boundary for superiority of tivozanib/mFOLFOX6 over bevacizumab/mFOLFOX6 for PFS in the intent-to-treat population was crossed; median PFS was 9.4 versus 10.7 months
The median PFS of the whole group was 3.9 months (95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.1-5.9).

efficacy.model: Human colorectal patient-derived xenografts (PDX) in mice
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read via scrape; the colon PDX single-agent tumour-growth-inhibition number sits in Figure 6B, which was not read. The 2023 FDA review names no PDX study, so model_filed is false.
efficacy.note: Fruquintinib, alone and with oxaliplatin, was tested in the colon cancer PDX COL1T0117P4 (Sun 2014); no patient data yet for comparison.
efficacy.short: Colon PDX COL1T0117P4 dosed with fruquintinib
efficacy.quote: Similarly, the enhanced inhibitory effect of fruquintinib with oxaliplatin was seen in the colon cancer PDX model COL1T0117P4
efficacy.judgement: A PDX is a different system from the HT-29/LoVo cell-line xenografts on the crc-xenograft-rodent track (patient tumour, serially passaged, no cell-line adaptation), so it gets its own track.

efficacy.model: Human colorectal patient-derived xenografts (PDX) in mice
efficacy.magnitude_basis: PDX tumour growth inhibition (fruquintinib alone and with oxaliplatin, figure only) vs placebo-controlled PFS hazard ratio 0.30; not commensurable
efficacy.confidence_note: Pairing made here: Xu 2017 does not cite the PDX. Model side read in full text (scrape); trial side at abstract level, quote verbatim in the abstract.
efficacy.note: The colon PDX predicted fruquintinib activity; the placebo-controlled phase II in refractory mCRC met its PFS primary endpoint (HR 0.30).
efficacy.short: Phase II PFS HR 0.30 vs placebo
efficacy.quote: PFS was significantly improved with fruquintinib plus BSC (4.73 months; 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.86-5.59) versus placebo plus BSC (0.99 months; 95% CI 0.95-1.58); (hazard ratio [HR] 0.30; 95% CI 0.15-0.59; P < 0.001).
efficacy.judgement: Direction only: the PDX experiment was a combination with oxaliplatin and the trial was monotherapy versus placebo, so only the sign of single-agent activity transfers. Apatinib/rivoceranib was also run in CRC PDX (Jia 2018, doi 10.7150/jca.20964, with the cMet inhibitor volitinib) but its CRC patient data are single-arm only, so that drug changes nothing on this track. outcome_tested positive: FRESCO (NCT02314819) and FRESCO-2 (NCT04322539, results 2023-09-14) later confirmed on overall survival.

patient_trials.quote: The median OS was 7.72 versus 5.52 months (HR 0.71; 95% CI 0.38-1.34).

efficacy.model: Patient-derived mCRC spheroids, ex-vivo drug-sensitivity profiling (42-drug panel incl. tivozanib)
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC13168235, epub 2026-03-19). The anti-VEGFR comparison used 3 patients (ID1, ID5, ID12) whose anti-angiogenic therapy was bevacizumab-based.
efficacy.note: Tivozanib was one of 9 anti-VEGFR compounds screened; the source's stated discordance with clinic was against bevacizumab regimens, not a member drug.
efficacy.short: Spheroids screened with tivozanib; no member-drug patients
efficacy.quote: Sensitivity to anti-EGFR drugs distinguished responsive from resistant patients and revealed candidates for anti-ERBB2 therapy, whereas anti-VEGFR screening failed to recapitulate clinical outcomes.
efficacy.judgement: Untested, not contra: the only patient responses compared were to bevacizumab (anti-VEGF-A antibody, outside the member list) and regorafenib (multikinase, outside the list), so under the do-not-widen rule the member-class track has no admissible comparison. The source itself concludes that non-vascularised 3D models cannot read anti-angiogenic activity and drops VEGFR inhibitors from future panels.

efficacy.population: Colorectal cancer, 22 patients (chip-vs-clinic set); 5 patients for the small-molecule panel
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC13400167, first published 2026-06-17). Apatinib and fruquintinib were dosed on chips from five patients (Figure 6); the one drug-matched patient (P15) received regorafenib.
efficacy.note: Apatinib and fruquintinib were tested on patient chips; the 86% chip-vs-clinic accuracy was for FOLFOX plus bevacizumab, and the one followed patient got regorafenib.
efficacy.short: Chips dosed with apatinib/fruquintinib; patients got bevacizumab
efficacy.quote: This study confirms the effectiveness of this model and verifies the variation in the response of tumoroid-on-a-chip models from different patients to FOLFOX plus bevacizumab.
efficacy.judgement: A separate system from the spheroids: self-assembled tumour vasculature under perfusion is the feature the spheroid paper lacked. Untested for this class because no patient in the study received fruquintinib or apatinib; the clinical concordance claim is for bevacizumab plus FOLFOX and the drug-matched case is regorafenib, both outside the member list.

safety.judgement: Proxy opening entry (PK paper, not a tox paper): it is the first public use of the species package for a class member in this program.
safety.model: Rat, dog and monkey PK/toxicology package (fruquintinib)
safety.note: Species package in use for fruquintinib; toxicology and safety-pharmacology findings stayed unpublished until the 2023 FDA review, so no comparison was possible.
safety.short: Species package in use; tox unpublished
safety.quote: It shows moderate oral bioavailability of 42-53 % and Tmax < 4 h in mouse, rat, dog and monkey, with exposure-dose linearity proved in rats and dogs.

safety.magnitude_basis: dose multiple at which hypertension appeared: 3 mg/kg in monkeys = 39-fold the recommended human dose (review's own HED), vs hypertension in 454/1008 (45%) RCC patients at 1x
safety.confidence_note: Patient side is RCC (review: 'Hypertension occurred in 454/1008 (45%) of patients with RCC treated with tivozanib at the proposed dose'); BATON-CRC's abstract says adverse events matched previous tivozanib studies but does not itemise hypertension.
safety.judgement: Same in direction (the harm was predicted) with a badly misplaced margin: the review puts the monkey effect at 39x the human dose, while patients were hypertensive at the clinical dose. Imported from RCC because the itemised patient data are from the RCC NDA.
safety.note: Monkey telemetry raised blood pressure at 3 mg/kg (39x the human dose); 45% of tivozanib RCC patients became hypertensive at the clinical dose.
safety.short: Monkey BP rise predicted hypertension, margin 39x
safety.quote: A dose of 3 mg/kg resulted in increases in systolic, diastolic and mean arterial blood pressure 90 minutes post-dose.

safety.magnitude_basis: missed harm; no model number to scale (patient side: 'The most common Grade 3-4 AE was hypertension, which occurred more frequently on the fruquintinib arm relative to placebo (14% vs. 1%)')
safety.confidence_note: The dog cardiovascular study was single-dose (up to 0.34 mg/kg, about 2x the clinical dose on BSA), a design that cannot show a harm that takes days to develop; the 13-week dog study reported no blood-pressure data. Scored as silence contradicted because monkeys (tivozanib) and dogs can show VEGFR-TKI hypertension. The package did predict haemorrhage (rat adrenal haemorrhage, dog red faeces/discharge), physeal thickening and embryo-fetal toxicity, which hold in the label.
safety.judgement: One drug's contra beats another's same on the same track, so the tox track ends contra despite the tivozanib monkey match; the two drugs' non-rodent species differ (monkey vs dog), which is the main reason this could instead be split into two tracks. Proteinuria and hand-foot syndrome were also unpredicted but are not separately scored.
safety.model: Dog cardiovascular safety pharmacology and 13-week rat/dog toxicology (fruquintinib)
safety.note: Dog telemetry and 13-week rat/dog studies were silent on blood pressure; hypertension was the most common grade 3-4 event in FRESCO-2 (14% vs 1%).
safety.quote: Fruquintinib did not have any toxicologically significant effects on cardiovascular function following a single oral dose up to 0.34 mg/kg.
safety.reason: Hypertension missed by dog CV studies
